newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban loses town, fights for airbase.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban loses town, fights for airbase.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban government said on Sunday it had lost control of an important town to opposition forces but was fighting for a nearby airbase north of Kabul.
The Afghan capital was itself hit in an air raid.

The opposition alliance had earlier said its forces captured Charikar town, capital of Parwan Province 64 km (40 miles) from Kabul, on Saturday night and Bagram airbase on Sunday morning in a rout for the fundamentalist Taleban.
Taleban spokesmen confirmed their Islamic militia had retreated from Charikar, but said it had repulsed the attack on Bagram while expecting reinforcements to arrive.
As fighting raged north of Kabul, an opposition jet bombed a suburb of the capital at midday, killing at least seven people and wounding 12, residents at the scene said.
Most dead and wounded came from a house where the owner was hosting a lunch for his friends and relatives, one said.

Official Kabul radio, monitored in neighbouring Pakistan, said: "For the sake of saving people's life and property, the (Taleban) Islamic forces made a tactical retreat from Charikar to strong and fortified positions."
It said the Taleban repulsed the attack on Bagram and inflicted heavy casualties on the attackers.
An opposition spokesman said earlier: "We captured Charikar at 9 p.m. (1630 gmt) on Saturday night and Bagram airbase at 9 this morning (0430 gmt)."
An official of the government ousted by Taleban from Kabul last September told Reuters: "We closed the road and the Taleban could not withdraw any of their vehicles or equipment."
He said 500 Taleban fighters had been killed.
The official, who did not want to be named, was speaking by satellite telephone from the Panjsher valley stronghold of the ex-government's senior military commander, Ahmed Shah Masood.

A Pakistan-based private Afghan news service quoted a Taleban official in the southern town of Kandahar as saying that about 1,000 fighters had been sent from there to reinforce the frontline north of Kabul.
Charikar fell to the Taleban in January, but has been under pressure from opposition forces for more than a month since they took the town of Jabal os-Siraj 70 km (45 miles) north of Kabul.
Charikar controls access to the Ghorband valley, where the Taleban are fighting forces of the Hezb-e-Wahdat faction, a mainly Shi'ite Moslem party in the opposition alliance.

Bagram has long been Kabul's main military airfield, and was used by Soviet occupation forces against mujahideen guerrillas in the 1980s, but it has been out of action for 10 months because it was too close to the front line.
The Taleban forces have been under continuous pressure since they briefly captured most of the opposition-held north in May.
They have been gradually losing ground ever since. But they still control most of Afghanistan and are the most formidable single force in the country.
